To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the MUC1 inhibitor GO-203 suppresses the TIGAR protein and inhibits the growth of colon cancers in vitro and in vivo.
the MUC1 inhibitor GO-203 inhibits TIGAR translation and suppresses the growth of colorectal cancer cells in vitro as well as in xenograft tumors.
targeting MUC-C inhibits the TIGAR translation and thus the AKT-SGK1 pathway regulating TIGA protein level in colorectal cancer cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of MUC1 inhibition on TIGAR expression and its implications for colorectal cancer.
the role of MUC1 in the regulation of the TIGAR pathway, and the potential of MUC1 inhibitors to treat colon cancer.
the role of MUC1 in cancer and the development of MUC1 inhibitors for cancer therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
targeting the MUC1 heteromeric protein, and specifically the MUC1-CA subunit, is a promising strategy for the treatment of colon cancer.
